description: Decomposition of the generalisation_v1 prediction errors by established determinant, k-mer representation of that determinant, mechanism and population novelty, and phenotype and genome quality, with a point-mutation augmentation sensitivity analysis on the frozen splits

catalogue.source: every rule of determinant mapping v1 for a study antimicrobial; mechanism class from the rules below; point-mutation loci from the AMRFinderPlus 2026-08-07.1 mutation tables; gene function from AMRFinderPlus fam.tsv family names

mechanism_classes.note: a point mutation in a gene not listed here is a catalogue error

drug_groups.statistic: largest pooled drop over the drug's holdouts (lineage, country, project, geography, temporal), same test isolates
drug_groups.note: case studies are every primary drug in the high_loss or stable group; all drugs are analysed quantitatively

capture.definition: a determinant is captured when at least one PR #14 kept feature k-mer encodes it in that genome: for a gene, a kept k-mer inside the called gene; for a point mutation, a kept k-mer overlapping a changed base of the mutant allele. Partially represented: no such kept k-mer, but a mutant-allele k-mer is sampled (and pruned), or a wild-type-allele k-mer at the site is kept, so the mutation shows only as the absence of a wild-type feature. Not represented: no sampled k-mer at the site for either allele (gene: no sampled k-mer in the gene). Unknown: the site could not be located. Phenotype and model output are never read.

novelty.definition: a determinant is seen in training when at least 5 training endpoints of the task carry it (any phenotype; 5 is the PR #14 feature minimum); an endpoint's mechanism is seen when all its established determinants are, unseen otherwise; DET- endpoints have no established mechanism; the exact determinant combination is seen when at least one training endpoint carries it

augmentation.indicators: one 0/1 column per catalogue point mutation with a predicts_resistance or component rule for any study drug, set from the AMRFinderPlus calls (partial hits excluded); the same columns for every drug
augmentation.eligibility: a drug is refitted when its catalogue has a point-mutation rule, at least 20 common-cohort endpoints carry such a mutation and fewer than 90% of those carriers have it captured by the PR #14 features
augmentation.control: the indicator block with its rows permuted across isolates (seed below), keeping prevalence and co-occurrence but breaking the link to each genome
augmentation.model: the PR #14 model, C grid, inner CV, seeds, feature filter and threshold, unchanged
